errors.text: The hypothesis substitutes atmospheric macroscopic sliding and tribo-oxidation for the target's nanoindentation/friction simulation of an FeNiCrCoCu coating on single-crystal Cu.
The proposed boundary of approximately 800 degrees Celsius is substantially different from the target boundary of 900 K, approximately 627 degrees Celsius.
The predicted improvement up to 800 degrees Celsius conflicts with the target result, where hardness and wear resistance are roughly stable only through 600 K and deteriorate sharply at 900 K.

The dominant mechanisms proposed—protective oxidation, sigma precipitation, thermal-mismatch cracking, and coating delamination—are absent from the target, which attributes degradation to lattice disorder, loss of dislocation density, softening, and a change from stacking-fault-mediated deformation.

The cited phase-transition evidence concerns different HEA compositions and high-pressure or long-term annealing conditions, so it does not establish the proposed transformation mechanism in the target coating.
